## bc005ea27dae

Generator SHA256: `7381145e452b148a4f0f160c647af6b3a1a2aa2b999cd33676842ae5efd9250e`.
Rule ID: `69c560267beb`. Exact executed canonical rule-source SHA256: `69c560267bebaa735a17bcc49fcbb99ceb3e3eda03089dc3c9eac403e86e78bb`.

**A2.1 — reproduced silent object loss.** 7/192 draws contain fewer than the promised minimum three separated objects. All 192 inputs are unique and accepted by `self_check`. The placement loop can exhaust its bounded retry budget and continue without placing a planned shape, so planned object counts need not match the realized input.

**A2.2 — reproduced loss of strict perimeter maximum.** 7/192 draws have no strictly largest edge-perimeter object despite the intended strict-max sampling condition. These are not 14 asserted distinct bad inputs; categories can overlap. The saved first witness for both findings is **easy, seed 5, sample index 1005, no overrides**: only two components remain, a color-5 object with area 8 and exposed-edge perimeter 12, and a color-4 object with area 5 and perimeter 12. See `witnesses.dropped_components` and `witnesses.perimeter_tie` in `checks/audits/bc005ea27dae.json`.

The actual reference output is the saved 2×4 all-8 grid; the authority's area tie-break chooses deterministically. Therefore the finding is not label ambiguity or a reference crash. It is failure to preserve the generator's narrower “three or more objects, strict perimeter winner” teaching distribution after allocation. The generator's perimeter implementation counts exposed edges correctly; no edge-count versus boundary-cell implementation mismatch is claimed.

Suggested future repair: validate counts, separateness and the winner on the actual rendered grid; resample or fail explicitly if a planned shape was dropped. Re-check the strict maximum after all placement, not solely before it. If ties are desired teaching cases, expose them as an intentional profile with appropriate witnesses rather than accidental leakage.

**A2.3 — reproduced ignored overrides.** At **medium, seed 7, sample index 19**, request `grid_h=9, grid_w=11, n_objects=6`. Actual output input is **14×17 with three components**, byte-for-byte equal to the no-override draw. It is validator-accepted and reference-executable. Full grids and output are saved under `witnesses.ignored_overrides`.

**Checked nonfailures and limits.** All three canonical pairs pass the validator and match actual Racket output. This audit did not establish a transformation shortcut or any incorrect Racket label; it found reproducible placement and requested-axis contract defects. No source changes, approval changes or automatic admission are included for either audit target.

triage.reason: Brief-reviewed under October 3 lightweight policy; preserve reported evidence and findings. Shared-tool requests consolidated separately. No maintainer battery/test/private-solve rerun or automatic training admission.

## bc005ea27dae

**Reproduced defect — generator violates its strict-maximum premise.** On the
documented default domain at `difficulty=easy`, seed `10055`, sample index `55`,
the generator emits three components with perimeters 12, 10, and 12. Its
`self_check` returns no errors even though two components tie for the maximum.
The selected Racket rule resolves the tie by traversal order and returns the
first component; a plausible bottom-right tie resolver returns the other tied
component, so the outputs differ.

The exact input, component measurements, hashes, rival output, and replay command
are in `checks/audit/bc005ea27dae/counterexample.json`; the supported Racket
result is `checks/audit/bc005ea27dae/racket.json`. Generator SHA-256 is
`7381145e452b148a4f0f160c647af6b3a1a2aa2b999cd33676842ae5efd9250e`,
executed rule hash is `69c560267beb`, and the input passes the target validator.
No audit-target source was changed.
